data.description:
## Why
A parallel session found reconciler operations HAND-ROLLING git commit/push against the tickets tracker instead of using the shared atomic commit+push seam (src/rebar/_store/event_commit_git.py + _push_policy.py). That session is remediating the instances; THIS ticket owns the gate gap: nothing in lint or CI detects a tracker-mutating git call added outside the sanctioned seam, which is how these instances landed unnoticed. This is the enforcement follow-on to the closed dirtiness/wedge lane (small-delicious-loris, compulsory-pernickety-mantis): those fixed the crash-atomicity of the seam itself; an unsanctioned bypass reintroduces the same dirty-tree/wedge class the lane closed.

## Mechanism: shrink-only seam ratchet (mirrors the complexity-baseline pattern)
1. New checker `scripts/check_git_seam.py`: AST-scan `src/rebar` for subprocess invocations whose argv starts with `git` (subprocess.run/check_output/Popen and the repo's local wrappers) reached with a `commit`, `push`, `add`, `rm`, `restore`, or `stash` subcommand; classify each call site by module.
2. Sanctioned allowlist (in the script, reviewed in-diff): `src/rebar/_store/` (the seam) plus an explicit frozen-baseline list of today's known out-of-seam sites (the instances the parallel session is draining, enumerated at implementation time from the scan itself).
3. Shrink-only: any NEW out-of-seam site fails; a removed site must leave the baseline (stale entry fails, like the complexity ratchet) so the debt only drains. When the parallel session's remediation lands, its sites leave the baseline in the same change or a trivial follow-up.
4. Wire into `make lint` (operation-linked, so it runs locally and under ANY CI provider — no CI-specific trigger), alongside check_complexity_baseline.py.
5. Unit tests: a fixture module with a raw `subprocess.run(["git","commit",...])` is flagged; a call through the seam is not; baseline add/remove semantics (new fails, stale fails, unchanged passes).

## Non-goals
Remediating the existing hand-rolled instances (parallel session owns that); runtime interception; non-git subprocess policy.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `scripts/check_git_seam.py` exists; AST-based (not grep), covers subprocess.run/check_output/check_call/Popen and local `_run_git`-style wrappers that shell to git, detecting mutating subcommands (commit, push, add, rm, restore, stash).
- [ ] Allowlist = `src/rebar/_store/` seam modules + frozen baseline of current out-of-seam sites captured from the initial scan; baseline is shrink-only (new site fails, stale entry fails, drain passes).
- [ ] `make lint` runs the checker; a seeded new out-of-seam call in a scratch module fails it (demonstrated in tests, not by committing a violation).
- [ ] Unit tests cover: flagged raw call, seam call not flagged, wrapper call flagged, baseline new/stale/unchanged semantics.
- [ ] Checker passes on the CURRENT tree (baseline captured honestly; zero suppressions outside the baseline file).
- [ ] `make lint` / `make typecheck` clean; lands via Gerrit (LLM-Review +1, Verified +1).
data.title: Gate: shrink-only ratchet forbidding tracker git mutations outside the _store seam
